takeaway: Addison's disease: adrenal insufficiency with low blood pressure and high potassium, often autoimmune and linked to pernicious anaemia.

question.text: A 30-year-old woman with pernicious anaemia has dizzy spells, fatigue and lethargy. Her BP is low and her potassium is high. Likely diagnosis?
question.say: A thirty-year-old woman with known pernicious anaemia has dizzy spells, fatigue and lethargy. Her investigations show a low blood pressure and a high serum potassium. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.text: A 30-year-old woman who is dizzy, tired and lethargic.
lines.say: This thirty-year-old woman is dizzy, tired and lethargic.
She has known pernicious anaemia, an autoimmune condition.

lines.text: The potassium is high: the banana king!
lines.say: (laugh) And her serum potassium is high. The banana is crowned king!

lines.text: The tired adrenals fail: adrenocortical insufficiency.
lines.say: The tired adrenals are failing. This is adrenocortical insufficiency, called Addison's disease.

lines.text: In 60 per cent of cases it is autoimmune, linked to other autoimmune diseases.
lines.say: In sixty per cent of cases it is autoimmune, and it is associated with other autoimmune conditions.

lines.text: Remember: low blood pressure, high potassium and pernicious anaemia mean Addison's disease.
lines.say: Remember: low blood pressure, high potassium and pernicious anaemia mean Addison's disease.
